# `set_sensor_calibration`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Write balance-sensor and/or compass-sensor calibration values.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build, command-socket invocation); 32-bit build probable |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, set_sensor_calibration @0xdc460, SetGsenCalibration @0x123c60 |

Replaces calibration values and persists them to configuration. The balance sensor is replaced wholesale from the supplied members; the compass sensor is patched with the float-typed members present. The handler ignores configuration write and sentinel failures and still reports success, so a success reply does not guarantee that every member was stored.

Side effects: Writes balance components sequentially to globals and configuration and sets its exist flag to the aggregate success; sets the compass exist flag and writes the supplied members individually. Partial changes can survive an ignored failure. Every full call also makes the shared diagnostic log writes.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_sensor_calibration"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Top-level object required: absent, null, scalar and array params (including an array holding an object) give 107. Unknown members ignored. Neither nested object reads exist. [READ] |
| `params.balanceSensor` | object | no | - | Balance sensor replacement values. A non-object is treated as empty. Each occurrence REPLACES the stored values (not a patch): omitted x defaults to -999 (the sentinel, which invalidates the sensor's exist flag), omitted y and z default to 0. A component within 0.1 of -999 is rejected inside the helper (209 set internally, ignored by the handler). [READ] |
| `params.balanceSensor.x` | number | no | -999 | X offset, number (integer or float); default -999. [READ] |
| `params.balanceSensor.y` | number | no | 0 | Y offset, number; default 0. [READ] |
| `params.balanceSensor.z` | number | no | 0 | Z offset, number; default 0. [READ] |
| `params.compassSensor` | object | no | - | Compass sensor values. Presence alone sets the sensor's exist flag true, even for empty or malformed input. Each member is read ONLY when it is a JSON float token; integer-valued tokens (such as 1) are ignored, and missing or ignored members retain the stored value. [READ] |
| `params.compassSensor.x` | number | no | - | Compass calibration value, float token only; units not established. [READ] |
| `params.compassSensor.y` | number | no | - | Compass calibration value, float token only; units not established. [READ] |
| `params.compassSensor.z` | number | no | - | Compass calibration value, float token only; units not established. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params is not an object | `expected object param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Sentinel (-999) rejection and configuration-write failures are swallowed: the reply is still result 0.

## Example

Request, set - Set both sensors (shape per static analysis; values invented):

```json
{"id":62,"method":"set_sensor_calibration","params":{"balanceSensor":{"x":0.5,"y":0.25,"z":9.5},"compassSensor":{"x":1.5,"y":-2.5,"z":3.5,"x11":1.25,"x12":0.5,"y11":0.5,"y12":1.25}}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_sensor_calibration","result":0,"code":0,"id":62}
```

Reply, not-object:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_sensor_calibration","error":"expected object param","code":107,"id":63}
```
